subject: geography
title: Coastal Landforms
welcome_lead: Head to the seaside! Waves are powerful sculptors. Discover how they carve cliffs, caves, arches and stacks.
meta_desc: KS3 Geography adventure on coastal landforms including cliffs, caves, arches, stacks and spits.
final_note: Awesome! You can now identify key coastal features made by waves.

concepts.def: Steep rock face along the coast.
Hollow formed at the base of a cliff.
Rock bridge formed when caves meet.
Tall rock pillar left when arch collapses.
Long sand ridge stretching into the sea.
Movement of sand along the coast by waves.

walkthroughs.body_html: Waves attack a weak crack in a cliff. The crack grows into a cave. The cave breaks through to form an arch. When the arch collapses, a stack is left standing alone.
Waves hit the beach at an angle and push sand along the coast — this is longshore drift. Where the coastline bends, sand builds out into the sea forming a spit.
The Old Harry Rocks in Dorset show stacks beautifully. Spurn Point is a famous UK spit.

mcqs.q: In a tropical rainforest nutrient cycle, where is most of the nutrient stored?
options: In the biomass (living plants). Litter is rapidly decomposed by warm humid conditions, and soil is leached — so cycling between biomass and litter dominates.
Walker circulation is the rotation of the Earth around the sun.
Most nutrients in a rainforest are stored in the soil — that's why plants grow so well.
Most rainforest nutrients are stored in animals.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between mitigation and adaptation to climate change?
options: Mitigation reduces the causes (cutting greenhouse gas emissions); adaptation reduces the impacts (e.g. building sea walls, drought-resistant crops, early warning systems).
Mitigation and adaptation mean the same thing — both are about stopping climate change.
Mitigation is done by HICs and adaptation is done by LICs.
Walker circulation is the rotation of the Earth around the sun.

mcqs.q: What is the Walker circulation and how does ENSO disrupt it?
options: Walker circulation is the east-west tropical Pacific atmospheric loop: trade winds push warm water west, air rises in Indonesia, sinks over Peru. El Nino weakens it, La Nina strengthens it.
Walker circulation is the rotation of the Earth around the sun.
El Nino is a current that flows from Peru to Australia.
Mitigation is done by HICs and adaptation is done by LICs.
